current.text: He signed a new contract this offseason.
He is projected to start for Detroit next to Cade Cunningham, Duncan Robinson, John Collins and Jalen Duren.
Coach J.B. Bickerstaff says he will play more than 26 minutes a game.

Experts do not trust Bickerstaff's comments on his minutes, because Bickerstaff has misled about Thompson's minutes and health before. They still expect more minutes, most often two to four more a game. Dan says the staff can no longer keep such a disruptive defender off the floor.
He averaged 32 minutes over Detroit's last 12 playoff games, and all sides agreed he must play a lot.
The front office wants him on the ball more. Some of Tobias Harris's old usage is meant to go to him, and Detroit lost creation with Harris gone.
His jump shot was rebuilt. The team expects about three three-point attempts a game and more midrange shots from him.

Most experts expect his scoring and assists to rise, with about one more assist a game and around 4 assists. One hopeful line is 6 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 2 steals and 1 block on 54% shooting, with no threes and low scoring. Dan does not expect him to improve much as a player and rests the case on minutes.
At 26 minutes he may not beat his ADP. At 28 to 30 minutes he should beat it easily. Better three-point shooting plus more usage, assists and minutes would give him top 50 upside.
His best case is about 28th overall, likely from a big steals season. The downside includes his free throws staying dreadful.
Experts call him underpriced and a steal in category leagues. They would draft him in the 50s or 60s, above an ADP in the 80s, and name him the top fantasy target on the Pistons.
He went for 17 USD in an expert auction mock draft.
Josh could see him going for up to 20 USD in an auction.
Josh still has concerns about his fit next to Jalen Duren.
If the plan to put him and Duren on the ball is failing by January, Detroit may trade for a secondary playmaker at the deadline, which would cut his usage.
Detroit plays 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21 and has 15 back-to-backs this season.
No rest risk is expected for Detroit players in back-to-backs.

durable.text: He is an elite defender. His fantasy value comes mainly from steals, backed by good blocks for a wing. He is a consistent steals producer with a high deflection rate.
He is a very poor free-throw shooter and makes almost no threes. His two-point shooting is okay.
He is a solid rebounder for his position.
His efficiency on self-created plays is well below league average.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.

note: He is a steals anchor (2.0 per game, z +3.4) with good blocks and solid FG%, but his FT% (about 59%) and near-zero threes make him a clear punt FT% and punt 3PM fit. Yahoo values him at 14 USD and ESPN at 4 USD, he cost 16 USD in our league last season and 17 USD in an expert mock, so about 14 to 18 USD is fair and the experts see upside above that. Early in the season, check whether he plays 28 or more minutes and whether his assists and three-point attempts rise, because the case for him rests on that.
